hook_text: Three ideas on three sheets. Two drawings each. One table decides.
clip_script: Every idea gets two drawings. Insides: a circuit diagram, proper symbols, every value written, LED the right way round. Trace it: when the tank drops, does the LED light? Outside: a pencil sketch of the box on the sill and the sensor on the tank, every part from the diagram placed inside, a hand for scale. Then the table: specifications down, ideas across, tick or cross. Reed switch needs no hole and no standby current. Flashing LED is seen at ten metres. Probes corrode. Combine the best: sealed reed switch, flashing LED, simple series circuit. Write why with the specification numbers. Redraw clean. Done.
visual_style: Whiteboard split: a circuit diagram with values on the left, a box sketch on the right; a tick table filling in below; arrows pulling the best parts into one final sheet.
mood: Organised and collaborative, like a design review.
pacing: Two drawings, trace, sketch, table, best bits, reasons, clean.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the circuit and the box for a night light idea.
